title: Place the user age key declaratively from the bootstrap sops file
description:
Provisioning a machine currently requires copying two age key files onto the new root by hand: /var/lib/sops-nix/keys.txt for NixOS and ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt for Home Manager. Neither sops module creates them — workstation/sops.nix sets generateKey to false and both set sshKeyPaths to the empty list, so they only point at a path that must already exist.

The second copy is avoidable. sops/bootstrap/host-key.yaml lists the shared host key as a recipient of itself, so the NixOS system key can decrypt it. Declaring it as a sops.secrets entry owned by the primary user puts the same key at a readable path, and Home Manager can point at that instead of a file in the home directory.

Only the system key then has to be seeded, which is irreducible: something has to put the first key on the machine.
design:
Do not aim the secret's path at ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt. sops-install-secrets creates missing parent directories as root (main.go MkdirAll around line 261), which would leave a root-owned ~/.config for Home Manager to fight over. Use the default /run/secrets/<name> location and repoint sops.age.keyFile at it instead.

Gate the repointing on isNixos and on sops.ageKey being default: standalone Home Manager has no /run/secrets, and the yubikey/tpm escape hatches must keep reading their own identity files.

No change in exposure — the key is already readable by this user at ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt today.
acceptance_criteria: A NixOS machine needs no age key in the home directory; docs/new-machine.md drops the second copy; standalone home-manager and the yubikey/tpm ageKey settings still resolve to ~/.config/sops/age/*.txt; all machines evaluate.
close_reason: modules/sops declares sops.secrets.host-age-key and points home-manager keyFile at it; verified for shared/yubikey/tpm/standalone

title: Write a new-machine provisioning runbook
description:
AGENTS.md documents adding a machine to the repo (create the directory, register it in machines.nix, run just bootstrap) but nothing covers going from bare hardware to a running system. Several steps are undocumented and at least one of them fails silently.

Missing steps, in the order they bite:
- Firmware must be put in Setup Mode before the first rebuild. lib/mkNixosConfiguration.nix defaults enableSecureBoot to true, and modules/secure-boot sets autoEnrollKeys with autoReboot, so key enrollment fails if the platform keys are still present.
- Cloning the repo on the installer requires network plus the wallet YubiKey, and must happen before any secret is available.
- The flake only sees git-tracked files, so a new machines/<host>/ directory must be git added before nixos-install or nixos-rebuild.
- TPM enrolment for LUKS auto-unlock exists only as a comment in modules/secure-boot/default.nix line 35.
- Post-install steps (tailscale up, sbctl verify) are not written down anywhere.
acceptance_criteria: docs/new-machine.md covers firmware prep through post-install verification; AGENTS.md and README.org link to it.
close_reason: docs/new-machine.md written; just new-machine + scripts/new-machine.sh added; README hostnames and structure corrected

title: Declare disk layout with disko for new machines
description:
Provisioning a new NixOS machine currently requires hand-partitioning: parted, cryptsetup luksFormat, mkfs.btrfs, subvolume creation, and mounting, none of which is recorded anywhere in the repo. The layout only exists implicitly in each machine's generated hardware-configuration.nix. Add disko so the LUKS + btrfs layout is declared in Nix and a fresh install is one command.

Scope: add the disko flake input, expose its NixOS module from lib/mkNixosConfiguration.nix, and add a reusable layout at lib/disk-layouts/luks-btrfs.nix parameterised by device. New machines import machines/<host>/disk.nix; the existing three machines keep their generated hardware-configuration.nix because disko-generated fileSystems would conflict with the by-uuid definitions already there.
design: Keep the LUKS mapper named 'crypted' so modules/sleep-then-hibernate (boot.resumeDevice = /dev/mapper/crypted) and the existing machines stay consistent. Use subvolumes @, @home, @nix, @snapshots to match the desktop machine's existing convention. Size the ESP at 2G rather than the usual 512M: lanzaboote writes a unified kernel image per generation and configurationLimit is 10.
acceptance_criteria: lib/disk-layouts/luks-btrfs.nix exists and is parameterised by device; disko module reachable from every nixosConfiguration; nix flake check passes; existing three machines build unchanged.
close_reason: disko input wired, lib/disk-layouts/luks-btrfs.nix added; all four machine configs evaluate

title: Support lanzaboote measured boot for TPM-backed LUKS unlock
description:
TPM-backed LUKS unlock is currently a comment in modules/secure-boot/default.nix suggesting systemd-cryptenroll with --tpm2-pcrs=0+7. That binds the volume to static PCR values, which change on firmware updates and on Secure Boot key changes, so every such event means re-enrolling by hand.

Lanzaboote 1.1.0 added Measured Boot via systemd-pcrlock. The volume is bound to a policy rather than to fixed PCR values, and lanzaboote regenerates the measurements and updates the TPM policy on every nixos-rebuild, so enrolment happens once and survives updates.

Expose it through modules.secure-boot rather than having each machine reach for boot.lanzaboote directly.
design:
Off by default. systemd-pcrlock is experimental upstream and it sits in the boot path of every machine that turns it on, so an existing working machine must not acquire it from a rebuild.

configurationLimit has to drop to 8 when it is on: common/system/system.nix sets 10 and lanzaboote asserts <= 8 for measured boot (nix/modules/lanzaboote.nix line 430), a limit systemd-pcrlock imposes. Set it from the module under mkIf rather than making the operator remember.

Default pcrs to [ 0 4 7 ], which is what the upstream guide recommends; 1, 2 and 3 are documented as possibly flaky per machine.

Do not expose autoCryptenroll. It enrols without a PIN, and the upstream guide is explicit that an attended workstation should require a user secret in addition to the TPM. Enrolment stays a deliberate manual step.
acceptance_criteria: modules.secure-boot.measuredBoot.enable exists and is off by default; enabling it sets configurationLimit to 8; existing machines evaluate unchanged; docs/new-machine.md documents the one-time pcrlock enrolment and drops the PCR 0+7 recipe.
close_reason: modules.secure-boot.measuredBoot added (off by default, forces configurationLimit 8); docs and finish-install rewritten around one-time pcrlock enrolment

title: Wrap the install steps in a just recipe
description:
docs/new-machine.md steps 5 through 7 are six commands the operator retypes with the hostname and device substituted in, three of which are easy to get subtly wrong: the disko mode string, the age key copy, and the passwd that has to happen before /mnt is unmounted. Everything they need is derivable from the hostname, since the device is declared in machines/<hostname>/disk.nix.

Wrap them in a recipe, with the preflight checks that currently exist only as prose in the runbook.
design:
Read the device from config.disko.devices.disk.main.device rather than taking it as an argument, so it cannot disagree with disk.nix. Refuse to run for a machine with no disko config — the three pre-disko machines would otherwise get their disks formatted from a config that does not describe them.

Do every check that can fail before anything touches the disk, in particular the presence of /var/lib/sops-nix/keys.txt: discovering after the install that nothing decrypts means starting over. Require the operator to type the hostname to confirm, and show the device's size and model first.

Offer a mount mode so a failed nixos-install can be retried without reformatting.
acceptance_criteria: just install-machine <hostname> partitions, installs, sets the user password, seeds the system age key and copies the checkout; refuses on a non-disko machine, a missing age key, or an untracked machine directory; a second recipe covers the post-boot steps.
close_reason: just install-machine + finish-install added; preflight guards exercised

title: Add a just recipe to scaffold a new machine
description:
Adding a machine means hand-creating machines/<host>/default.nix, generating hardware-configuration.nix, adding an entry to machines/machines.nix and remembering to git add the result, because the flake only sees tracked files. Forgetting the git add produces a confusing 'is not tracked by Git' error at build time.

Add a just recipe that performs those steps for a given hostname and disk device, including writing a disk.nix from the shared disko layout.
acceptance_criteria: just new-machine <hostname> <device> creates the machine directory with default.nix, disk.nix and a hardware-configuration.nix limited to kernel modules, registers the machine in machines.nix, and git adds everything.
close_reason: docs/new-machine.md written; just new-machine + scripts/new-machine.sh added; README hostnames and structure corrected

title: Replace 1Password SSH agent with sops-provisioned key + systemd ssh-agent
description:
The 1Password SSH agent cannot be unlocked from a terminal, so SSH-ing into a machine leaves no usable agent there. Additionally, the global IdentityAgent setting in workstation/ssh.nix is deployed to every machine and overrides SSH_AUTH_SOCK, silently disabling agent forwarding.

Move the main SSH private key into sops (sops/home/secrets.yaml, key ssh/main), reference it from ssh_config via config.sops.secrets, run a plain systemd-user ssh-agent, load the key with a oneshot ordered after sops-nix.service, and switch git commit signing from op-ssh-sign to OpenSSH's built-in signer.
close_reason: Implemented: sops-provisioned SSH keys, systemd ssh-agent, declarative linger, OpenSSH commit signing

title: Consolidate to a single shared host age key bootstrapped via YubiKey
description:
Today each machine has its own age keypair (desktop, work-laptop, work-tmp) listed as a SOPS/git-agecrypt recipient. Adding a machine means generating a key, editing .sops.yaml and git-agecrypt.toml, and re-encrypting everything.

Replace this with one shared host age key whose private material is stored in the repo, encrypted with SOPS to the YubiKey recipient only. Provisioning a new machine then becomes: insert the YubiKey once, run a bootstrap recipe that decrypts the shared host key into ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt and /var/lib/sops-nix/keys.txt, after which all SOPS secrets and git-agecrypt files decrypt without the YubiKey.
notes:
Implemented, verified, not yet committed.

Shared host key: age16fr85m3cp4g92mpyrzl6p3lldqzqlfc5nnkxn9tv6qaszjhrj3dqusgece

Verified on work-laptop: sops/home/secrets.yaml, sops/bootstrap/host-key.yaml and both private/** blobs all decrypt with the shared key alone. nix flake check passes, home-manager activation package and the work-laptop NixOS toplevel both evaluate/build.

Two follow-ups for the operator:

1. Commit promptly. The re-encrypted private/** blobs were written straight into the index with git update-index, bypassing the clean filter. Until they are in HEAD, any git add on those paths runs the clean filter, which reuses the ciphertext in HEAD and silently restores the old recipients.

2. /var/lib/sops-nix/keys.txt on work-laptop still holds the previous key; installing it needs sudo. Nothing under modules/sops declares secrets today, so nothing breaks, but running just bootstrap-host-key will bring it in line.

Old history of private/** stays readable with the YubiKey, which is still a recipient of those older blobs. ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt.pre-shared-host-key.bak holds the previous work-tmp key as a convenience for reading old commits; it can be deleted once that is no longer wanted.
close_reason: Implemented and committed as 52b731a. Verified on work-laptop: sops/**, sops/bootstrap/host-key.yaml and both private/** blobs decrypt with the shared host key alone; nix flake check passes; home-manager activation package and the work-laptop NixOS toplevel build. just bootstrap runs end to end. Remaining machines (desktop, x13-laptop) each need just bootstrap-host-key once with the YubiKey.

title: Migrate low-sensitivity private data from git-crypt to git-agecrypt
description:
The repo currently uses two encryption systems with disjoint key material: SOPS (age keys, listed in .sops.yaml) for real secrets under sops/, and git-crypt (symmetric GPG-backed key) for low-sensitivity private data under secrets/ (SSH host addresses, AWS SSO config). The git-crypt key is separate key material that must be provisioned independently on every machine.

Migrate the git-crypt tree to git-agecrypt so both encryption systems share the same age recipients and identities. Also rename the directory and the Nix attribute from 'secrets' to 'private', since the contents are not secrets: they are private information that is acceptable to expose in the world-readable Nix store, unlike the SOPS-managed material.

Scope:
- secrets/ -> private/ (secrets.json -> hosts.json)
- .gitattributes: git-crypt filter -> git-agecrypt filter
- git-agecrypt.toml: recipients matching the age recipients in .sops.yaml
- Nix attribute 'secrets' -> 'private' in flake.nix, lib/mkHomeConfiguration.nix, lib/mkNixosConfiguration.nix, workstation/ssh.nix, workstation/home.nix
- Add git-agecrypt to home packages and document the per-checkout bootstrap
- Update AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md
notes:
Migration done and staged, not committed (global instruction: no commit without explicit user request).

Verified: staged blobs are age ciphertext, worktree plaintext intact, clean/smudge roundtrip works, nix build of homeConfigurations.oskar@x86_64-linux succeeds with resolved SSH HostNames and .aws/config, nix flake check --impure passes.

Follow-up worth noting: git history before this change still contains git-crypt-encrypted blobs, so the git-crypt symmetric key stays relevant for reading old commits. git-crypt is kept in home.packages for that reason. Removing it entirely would require a history rewrite.
close_reason: Migration complete: private/ encrypted with git-agecrypt using the same age recipients as .sops.yaml; nix build and nix flake check pass.

title: Migrate version-pinned sources to nvfetcher
description: Move version-pinned/manual-hash fetches (calibre-open-with, caveman-shrink, chrome-devtools-mcp, code-review-graph) and the two version-pinned emacs flake inputs (pgmacs, lsp-ltex-plus) to nvfetcher. Expose via pkgs.nvSources overlay; add just update-sources recipe; remove redundant flake inputs. HEAD-tracked emacs pkgs (claude-code-ide, gptel-quick, consult-mu) excluded - no upstream releases.
close_reason: nvfetcher migration complete; build + flake check green

title: Migrate code-review-graph from programs.claude-code.mcpServers (old) to programs.mcp.servers (new)
description:
code-review-graph.nix:71 is the last consumer of programs.claude-code.mcpServers after commit e09499f unified MCP config via programs.mcp.servers. Migration was missed because the file is commented out in default.nix:57.

Goal: move the mcpServers entry to programs.mcp.servers."code-review-graph" so opencode also picks it up. Coordinates with the agents.tools refactor (this entry becomes agents.tools.codeReviewGraph.mcpServers."code-review-graph").
acceptance_criteria: No references to programs.claude-code.mcpServers in workstation/agents/. code-review-graph appears in programs.mcp.servers when enable=true.

title: Refactor: mkMcpServer helper + extract package builds to packages/
description:
mcp-servers.nix has 7 server entries built 7 slightly-different ways. github-mcp and kagi hand-roll shell wrappers to inject sops secrets. caveman-shrink is wrapped inline at 5 callsites. kagimcp's 25-line Python build sits inside the registration file.

Goal: introduce mkMcpServer { name, command, args ? [], secretEnvFiles ? {}, shrink ? false } and mkEmacsStdioServer { name, initFunction, stopFunction }. Move kagimcp build to packages/kagimcp.nix; move chrome-devtools-mcp build (currently default.nix:11-28) to packages/chrome-devtools-mcp.nix. mcp-servers.nix becomes a registration file.
acceptance_criteria: No inline shell-script wrappers in mcp-servers.nix. No inline package builds. All 7 servers go through helper. github-mcp + kagi still receive their sops secrets. caveman-shrink wrapping preserved for the 5 currently-shrunk servers.

title: Refactor: rename agents docs to {both,claudeOnly,opencodeOnly} + fix AGENTS.md union
description:
Current naming is misleading: extraClaudeDocs means 'both', extraOpencodeDocs means 'opencode-only', extraClaudeOnlyDocs means 'claude-only'. Worse, ~/.agents/AGENTS.md (combined) excludes extraOpencodeDocs despite naming.

Goal: rename top-level options to agents.docs.{both, claudeOnly, opencodeOnly} (lists). Tool submodule's docs field appends to these. AGENTS.md becomes a true union (both + claudeOnly + opencodeOnly). claude-code context = both + claudeOnly. opencode context = both + opencodeOnly.

Touches: default.nix (options + fold), caveman.nix (extraOpencodeDocs -> docs.opencodeOnly), beads.nix (same), rtk.nix (extraClaudeDocs -> docs.both), subagents.nix (folded into default.nix per Candidate A).
acceptance_criteria: No references to extraClaudeDocs/extraOpencodeDocs/extraClaudeOnlyDocs in agents/. ~/.agents/AGENTS.md contains content from all three streams.

title: Refactor: introduce agents.tools.<name> submodule + central fold
description:
Workstation/agents/ tool integrations (caveman, rtk, beads, code-review-graph) lack a shared shape. code-review-graph is enabled by uncommenting default.nix:57; no module gates on enable; chrome-devtools-mcp build sits in default.nix while its registration is in mcp-servers.nix.

Goal: introduce typed submodule agents.tools.<name> with fields { enable (default true), packages, mcpServers, hooks, docs.{both,claudeOnly,opencodeOnly}, skills, activation }. default.nix filters by enable and folds active tools into programs.{claude-code,opencode,mcp}, home.packages, agents.extraSkillPaths, home.activation.

Edge cases (caveman hooksDir/statusLine, security-guidance enabledPlugins) bypass via direct programs.claude-code.settings.* gated on cfg.enable.

Pass-throughs (security-guidance.nix, subagents.nix) collapse into default.nix as inline declarations.
acceptance_criteria: agents.tools.caveman.enable = false; disables caveman entirely (no hooks, no docs, no packages). nix flake check passes. home-manager build evaluates. claude-code starts with all tools active when defaults preserved.

title: Migrate agent config to programs.claude-code / programs.opencode module options
description: Replace home.file/xdg.configFile writes in workstation/agents/{default,skills,caveman}.nix with typed module options (context, skills, hooksDir, settings). Enable programs.opencode. Verify with nix build .#packages.x86_64-linux.default.

title: Fix stale hostnames and structure in README.org
description: README.org tells the reader that <hostname> is one of x13-laptop, work-laptop or x1laptop. There is no x1laptop machine; the third one is desktop. The Structure section also lists a system/ directory that does not exist in the repo. Both mislead anyone following the quick start on a new machine.
acceptance_criteria: Hostname list matches machines/machines.nix; Structure section matches the actual top-level directories.
close_reason: docs/new-machine.md written; just new-machine + scripts/new-machine.sh added; README hostnames and structure corrected

title: Add wofi-based Proton Pass quick access launcher
description: Linux/COSMIC equivalent of CiTroNaK/Quick-Access-for-Pass (macOS menu-bar app). Global-hotkey floating search over Proton Pass items via proton-pass-cli, with field selection and clipboard copy with auto-clear. Implemented as a wofi script packaged with writeShellApplication and bound to a COSMIC keyboard shortcut.
notes: Prototype implemented at workstation/scripts/protonpass-wofi.sh, packaged as protonpassWofi (writeShellApplication) in workstation/home.nix Linux package set. Verified headlessly against the real vault with a stub picker: item index build across vaults with 15min cache, field menu, TOTP generation, multi-line note copy, cancel paths, refresh path, clipboard auto-clear. Remaining: interactive wofi smoke test under COSMIC and a COSMIC keyboard shortcut (existing custom shortcut file already binds Super+space to 1password quick access).
close_reason: Implemented, committed as bc372c2, and confirmed working: the wofi window renders under COSMIC and Super+space is bound to it.

value: nvfetcher manages version-pinned external sources (nvfetcher.toml -> _sources/generated.nix), exposed as the pkgs.nvSources overlay in lib/mkHomeConfiguration.nix and lib/mkNixosConfiguration.nix. Update with 'just update-sources' (nodejs on PATH for npm src.cmd entries). Covers: calibre-open-with, caveman-shrink, chrome-devtools-mcp, code-review-graph, pgmacs, lsp-ltex-plus. Decision: nvfetcher for release/version-pinned sources; HEAD-tracked emacs packages (claude-code-ide, gptel-quick, consult-mu) stay flake inputs because their upstreams publish no usable GitHub releases. Caveat: for npm packages nvfetcher only hashes the source tarball; buildNpmPackage's npmDepsHash (and chrome-devtools-mcp-lock.json) must still be regenerated by hand on a version bump.
